name: Aman Tokyo
address: Otemachi Tower, 1-5-6 Otemachi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 100-0004, Japan
tagline: Eighty-four suites at the top of Otemachi Tower, five minutes from Tokyo Station.
description:
Aman Tokyo occupies the upper floors of the Otemachi Tower, in the business district beside the Imperial Palace Gardens. It has 84 suites and signature suites, a 2,500 square metre spa and a 30-metre indoor pool, all looking over the skyline.

Guests arrive at a lobby that the hotel counts among the largest in Tokyo. Its design follows Japanese tradition, with ikebana displays, washi paper doors and engawa platforms, set against granite and wood. Tokyo Station is a five-minute drive from the tower, and the base of the building opens onto a small forest, the Otemachi Forest, where The Café by Aman sits among the trees.

All 84 accommodations are suites, laid out like a ryokan with shoji screens, sunken living areas, deep stone furo baths and floor-to-ceiling windows. The Deluxe Suite and the Garden View Suite measure 71 square metres, and the Tokyo Suite 77. Above them are the signature suites: the City Suite at 121 square metres, the Grand Suite at 141, the Panorama Suite at up to 139 on the corners of the building, and the Aman Suite at 157 square metres, the largest in the hotel. On clear days some of the views take in Mount Fuji beyond the Imperial Palace Gardens. Breakfast, in-room refreshments and the wellness facilities are included in every stay.

Four restaurants cover a wide range. Arva serves southern Italian cooking by Masakazu Hiraki, who trained in Venice. Musashi is an intimate counter of hinoki cypress where chef Musashi serves omakase sushi in the Edomae tradition. The Lounge by Aman is open all day for cocktails, seasonal afternoon tea and meals, and La Pâtisserie, on the second basement floor of the tower, is the first Aman patisserie, making breads and pastries.

The Aman Spa covers 2,500 square metres over two floors and has eight treatment rooms, onsen-style baths, steam rooms, yoga and Pilates studios and a fitness centre open around the clock. Every treatment begins with the Misogi experience, a Shinto purification ritual with water, and the signature journey combines a scrub of camphor, kuromoji and Japanese clay with a 90-minute shiatsu and western massage. Guests can also book zazen meditation led by a monk, or Japanese acupuncture.

The hotel suits those who want space and quiet in the middle of the city, with Tokyo Station close and Narita and Haneda a car ride away. The Aman team can arrange journeys on to Aman Kyoto and Amanemu.
